messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: GPU OOM spike detected in cluster us-east-1 / inference-pool-23. 35 container restarts in last 7m. Suggested runbook: /runbooks/prefill-oom (priority: P1)
oncall-anna: I'm paged, looking now. seeing a flurry of restarts on node group inference-pool-23-us-east-1a. pods keep going CrashLoopBackOff with SIGKILL from kernel OOM killer.
sre_tina: logs show OOM during prefill path — long prompt allocations ballooning KV/prefill buffer. sample log:
```
W03 11:12:25.432 runtime_prefill.cpp:214] prefill allocate(3244032 bytes) failed
E03 11:12:25.437 cuda_runtime.cpp:98] CUDA Error: out of memory while allocating 3.2GB (device 0)
kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 41234 (containerd) score 925 or sacrifice child
```
eng-runtime-ryan: confirms. It's not a one-off noisy neighbor — token distribution shows many requests with >120k prefill tokens (huge). Prefill is trying to materialize KV cache for full context and blowing RAM.
oncall-anna: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce accepted prefill window on the loadbalancer 2) scale up cold fallback pool 3) cordon/drain the worst nodes to stop churn 4) route traffic to smaller model variant. doing (1) now.
support-jay: customer-impact: support queue shows 8 customers with errors/partial outputs — most are large-context chat apps. Ticket INC-2026-042 created. Informing top 3 affected accounts (gaming-inc, docsflow, research-labs) with ETA ~ 30m.
eng-runtime-ryan: run command I'm using:
```
# reduce max prefill tokens on gateway
kubectl -n control-plane patch config gateway-config -p '{"spec":{"max_prefill_tokens":4096}}' --type=merge
# scale cold fallback
kubectl -n inference scale deployment cold-fallback --replicas=6
```
oncall-anna: patched gateway to 4k tokens. immediate drop in new OOM events but existing pods still restarting.
sre_tina: cordoned node ip-10-0-14-23, draining to stop restarts and allow manual inspection: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-14-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
eng-runtime-ryan: rolling traffic to redwood-compact-v1 (smaller quantized variant) for the canary route. applying traffic rule:
```
route.add("/v1/generate", model="redwood-compact-v1", weight=1.0)
```
product-maria: we should notify customers about degraded responses and recommend reducing context length. drafting outbound now.
support-jay: sent initial notifications to affected accounts. included suggested mitigations for users: trim context, chunk long docs, reduce system/prefix injection. customers have acknowledged; one asks for SLA credits.
oncall-anna: monitoring: token-inflight dropped by 28% after gateway change. container restarts went from 35 in 7m -> 3 in last 5m. looks stabilizing but we want a safer permanent fix.
eng-runtime-ryan: quick hotfix options discussed: A) validate and reject >X prefill tokens at gateway B) change allocator to use mapped memory and fallback to eviction C) enforce per-request KV cap (prefer A now, fastest)
oncall-anna: implemented rejection rule at edge to 4k and added explicit error message to clients (`HTTP 413: prefill too large`). Rolling now.
sre_tina: still seeing a couple of CUDA OOM traces on older node types (driver 515). looks like heterogeneous fleet causing low headroom. spinning up a couple of larger instances (a100-like) in dedicated pool to absorb load.
eng-runtime-ryan: also pushing a follow-up patch to the runtime to pre-emptively trim longest prefix tokens when total prefill > limit. PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1892 (wip).
ops-lead-alex: good live coordination. next steps for incident postmortem: - root cause: insufficient prefill validation + heavy tail of extremely long prompts from a few customers - immediate mitigations: edge rejects, route to compact model, drain bad nodes - medium: runtime prefetch trimming + allocator hardening PR - long: quota and billing knobs for very large contexts + telemetry for request-size heatmaps
product-maria: writing customer summary and post-incident notes. please add any snippets I can copy.
sre_tina: diagnostics saved to S3: s3://redwood-incident-archive/1778001234/ (oom-dumps, dmesg, pod-logs)
eng-runtime-ryan: follow-up checklist in code:
- merge prefill-reject at gateway (hotfix)
- backfill tests for very long-context gen
- add metric `prefill_tokens_per_request` to dashboard
- add canary rule to route oversized to cold-model instead of trying allocation
oncall-anna: handing off to morning oncall @ops-lead-alex — system looks stable but please monitor for 2h. I'll update the runbook with what we did and timeline.
ops-lead-alex: taking over. noted to call out driver 515 nodes and consider rolling driver updates. marking incident as active -> mitigated. creating postmortem stub INC-2026-042-PM.
support-jay: capture draft to send customers: "We experienced an outage impacting large-context requests (>= ~8k tokens). We applied protective limits, routed traffic to a compact fallback, and are deploying runtime trims. Estimated full remediation in 48–72h." :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status changed: P1 -> mitigated by oncall-anna (1778001234). Runbook entry updated.
ops-lead-alex: final note: no data leakage observed, all restarts due to OOM. Thanks everyone for quick responses. will schedule postmortem review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. :coffee:
